utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. First of all, we are here now in a trial session. Yesterday we adjourned sine die, but I think from my last words yesterday, it was clear already that it might today that we would resume the trial proceedings today. Otherwise, we would have heard a deposition. Mr. McCloskey, I think we yesterday also briefly addressed that if Mr. Mladic would be back in court again, that you would draw your request for a deposition hearing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I take it that it is hereby withdrawn then.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is hereby withdrawn. Thank you. Mr. Lukic, the Chamber was informed that you would like to address the Chamber briefly in private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Could we briefly go in -- could we have the curtains down to go into closed session for the witness to enter the courtroom under the prevailing protective measures. Meanwhile, Mr. Lukic, I can indicate to you what kind of decisions are there to be read so that you -- yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Witness RM346, before you give evidence -- first of all, good morning. Before you give evidence, the Rules require that you make a solemn declaration. The text will now be handed out to you by the usher, and may I invite to you make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we start, I would like to inform you about a very practical matter. Usually we take breaks of some 20 minutes after a little bit over one hour. It might be that we need shorter breaks in between. Now, that may be breaks of only two or three minutes for very practical reasons. For you to leave the courtroom, curtains have to be down. Then you are escorted out of the courtroom. Getting back in the courtroom. That all takes quite some time. Therefore, for these very short breaks of only a few minutes, we suggest that you just stay in the courtroom. We'll stay in the courtroom. Everyone will stay in the courtroom, apart from the accused who will have to leave the courtroom then for a few minutes. If you would -- if that would be agreeable to you, we would proceed in that way.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then, of course, we would take a bit of a longer break after more than one hour. Thank you for your co-operative attitude. You'll first be examined by Ms. Hasan. Ms. Hasan is counsel for the Prosecution, and you'll find her to your right, Witness. Ms. Hasan, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: To begin, could we have 65 ter 28782 displayed for the witness and us in the courtroom and not broadcast for the public.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, take a look at the sheet before you and could you please confirm for us, without reading anything out loud, whether your name and your birth date is correctly recorded.

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'd offer then 65 ter 2872 [sic] into evidence under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 28782 receives number P1117, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted under seal. There is a little problem with the reading out of the number. I think Ms Hasan --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 28782, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 28782 was the document which is admitted as P1117, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, you've testified in this Tribunal already on three previous occasions. And in this case, too, could you just make sure that you're vigilant when I ask you or anyone asks you any questions not to reveal information that may reveal your identity, and if you feel required to do so, in answering the question, let us know and we will move into private session so that can you do so. Witness, can you tell us now, do you recall testifying in the Krstic case on the 14th of November, 2000, and in the Karadzic case on the 2nd of February in 2012?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Have you recently had the opportunity to review your prior testimony in those cases?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Are there any corrections to your prior testimony that you wish to make today?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So if I asked the very same questions you were asked, would you provide, in substance, the same answers?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now that you've taken the solemn declaration here before us, do you affirm that the testimony you gave in the Krstic and Karadzic cases was true and accurate, to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would then offer the testimony that was attached to our 8 March 2013 92 ter motion for this witness as exhibits in this case. That would be 65 ter 28783 for the Krstic testimony, and 65 ter 28784 for the excerpts from the Karadzic testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Registrar, the numbers would be? First 28783.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Receives number P1118, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Let me see, do we need to have it under seal?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not. No need to have it under seal. Therefore, admitted as a public document, public exhibit. 28784, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Receives number P1119, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P1119 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: For the benefit of the public, Mr. President, I'll read a brief summary of the witness's prior evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: On 11 July 1995, the witness' family left to Potocari. Afraid of being killed, he went to Jaglici. Approximately 10.000 to 15.000 people had gathered there. They decided to make their way to Tuzla. The witness left Jaglici on the afternoon of the 12th of July but was captured by Bosnian Serb soldiers near Nova Kasaba on the morning of the 13th of July. The witness was then held captive in an elementary school in Kasaba. In the afternoon, the Serb soldiers took him to a football field just outside Nova Kasaba. At this field he saw approximately 1.500 to 2.000 men surrounded by armed Serb soldiers. After a while, General Mladic arrived and delivered a speech to the prisoners. He also ordered that a list of their names be taken. One of the prisoners was beaten and shot to death by a Serb soldier. Later that same afternoon, buses arrived and took the prisoners. En route, near Sandici, the witness saw a group of men surrounded by Serb soldiers. Further on, near Kravica, the witness saw a hangar with four or five dead bodies at the entrance and he heard shooting coming from behind the hangar. The bus he was on stopped for the night in Bratunac, near a school. He heard shooting throughout the night. Several people were taken off the bus he was on and never came back. On the afternoon of 14 July, the prisoners were told that they would be exchanged. The witness and the other prisoners on his bus, along with four or five other buses, drove north in the direction of Zvornik, to a school in Pilica. The prisoners were ordered into a gym. There were other prisoners sitting and standing on the stairs leading up to the first floor of the school. Later that night, the witness volunteered to fetch water from a nearby water point. And while doing so, he heard a bus approach the school, followed by the sound of shots and people crying for help. The next day, on the 15th of July, Serb soldiers took personal belongings from the prisoners. And that night, men were taken out of the gym and did not return. On the morning of the 16th of July, the prisoners were told that the young men would be exchanged. The witness's hands were tied behind his back and he and other prisoners were put on the buses. The buses drove toward a meadow where the witness saw many dead bodies. He watched as the men from the first bus were taken out in groups of ten, escorted by three to four soldiers, who were taken to a meadow where they were subsequently shot and killed. The time came when he was ordered off his bus and he was taken to where the other bodies lay in the meadow. A group of ten soldiers shot at them and the witness, threw himself to the ground. He was shot in the back but the bullet passed under his left armpit and he survived. For the next approximately four hours, groups of prisoners continued to arrive to the meadow and they were killed. In the evening, a vehicle arrived and unloaded bodies at that site as well. The witness spent the night there and then escaped to a bridge where he hid the following day. During his journey, he encountered two other Muslim men whom he continued his escape with. Exhausted, the witness and the other Muslim man he was with turned themselves in at a later date. And, finally, on the 26th of December, in 1995, the witness was released. That concludes my summary. And if I may now proceed with my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, I'm just going to ask you a few questions that are going to just require us to go very briefly into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Perhaps you repeat the question for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: At approximately 2.00, after you had been imprisoned at these barracks at the elementary school in Nova Kasaba, you and the other men who had been captured with you were ordered to march towards what you have called a stadium, and you've also called it a football pitch which was just outside of Nova Kasaba. Could you describe in a little bit more detail what this field was?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: It was a sort of football pitch that had two goals. There were a couple of trees there. I think there were two sheds. There were benches for people to sit.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And when you refer to the stadium and this football pitch, are you referring to one and the same thing?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now when you arrived at this football pitch just outside Nova Kasaba, you say there were between approximately 1.500 to 2.000 prisoners there and these men were seated in rows. When you arrived at the field, were you -- were you ordered to sit with these men?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Was this also in rows or in some other formation?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: In rows.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, shortly after you arrived, you've testified that General Mladic arrived at the football field. Do you recall the vehicle General Mladic arrived in?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: Yes. I think it was some sort of jeep or APC. I'm not sure, really.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: You've previously testified that General Mladic delivered a speech to the prisoners as you sat there. How far away from General Mladic were you sitting when he gave his speech?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: Between 15 and 20 metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And you have previously testified that you had recognised him because you had seen him before and -- sorry, on television. And that you had been told by soldiers present at the field that he was expected. Do you remember if General Mladic also introduced himself at the beginning of his speech or at any time during his speech?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: I think that he did.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, you also testified about a prisoner amongst you who at some point stood up, was beaten by the soldiers there, and was shot and killed by one of the soldiers. Did you personally witness this incident?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And when you saw this prisoner get killed, was General Mladic still there?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Can you tell us approximately how long after this incident General Mladic left the football field?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. And ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: A pause, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll have a little pause, as was announced before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As I indicated before, we just show some patience for a couple of minutes, and then we'll proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I do not know whether you still have to consult with your client about the decisions to be read or whether there are some which are innocent enough?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think we can read these admissions of documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admission of documents. And that would be --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: P802 and P805.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then perhaps I briefly inform the witness. We'll use our time in court when waiting to read one or two decisions, so you don't have to be attentive to it. It's just to use our time as efficiently as possible. Yes, that can be delivered in open session, this decision. It is the -- the Chamber will now deliver its decision on the Prosecution's oral bar table motion to admit into evidence four documents with Exhibit numbers P802 up to and including P805. On the 24th of January, 2013, during the testimony of Witness Smith, the Prosecution intended to tender four documents through the witness. Following an indication by the Defence that it would object to the documents being admitted through the witness, the Prosecution, at the suggestion of the Chamber, tendered the said documents orally from the bar table. The Defence did not make further submissions in relation to this request. The relevant transcript pages are 7363, and P9507 to 9508. No, I'm -- it's not P; it's just transcript pages: 9507 to 9508. The Chamber will therefore now decide on the admission of P802 through P805. The Chamber analysed the four documents in light of Rule 89(C) and (D) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. All four documents are contemporaneous VRS documents that, taken together, create a full picture on how an order is processed within the VRS which may assist the Chamber in a better understanding of the VRS military chain of command. Moreover, Witness Smith testified about this subject matter. The Chamber considers all four documents to be relevant and reliable and, in light of the foregoing, admits P802 through P805 into evidence. And this concludes the Chamber's decision. Mr. Lukic, the admission of the report of Witness Patrick van der Weijden, would that be a decision that -- well, I think the witness -- Mr. Mladic returned to the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No loud speaking, Mr. Lukic [sic], as you are aware of. Ms. Hasan, if you are ready to continue. Witness, may I ask you, was -- we just heard the accused speaking. Was -- did you hear what he said? And was he addressing you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He most probably were -- was. Because he said that I had lied about it all. He said it was all lies. I don't know if he meant my statement, by I suppose so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you may make any submissions but the Chamber wants to remove Mr. Mladic from the courtroom now. If you have any different thing heard, then -- Mr. Mladic -- we stop recording. Curtains down. Curtains down. Mr. Mladic is removed from the courtroom. Mr. Mladic is removed from the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are in -- no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have the curtains up again. Mr. Mladic is not present in the courtroom anymore. Mr. Lukic, is there any challenge to the gist of what Mr. Mladic said? I'm not asking you to confirm that he said anything, but I'm just asking whether there's any challenge to the gist of what he said. If so, of course, we'll have to further investigate the matter, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As I heard it, and I did hear this time, he was addressing Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But was he talking aloud, was he saying that the witness had lied? Whomever he addressed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What I heard --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did he use the word "lies" or "lied" or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What I heard is that everything is learned by heart.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: He was commenting on the testimony of the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, no need to say that you will explain to your client that this type of comment which is inappropriate and, as he may have been aware of, leads to his removal from the courtroom. Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, just should it ever be necessary to review the tape that the Chamber has ordered be made, I would note that the comment was made at approximately 9 minutes past 10.00. The transcript doesn't record the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just see. The transcript doesn't record the time -- was it -- I was just listening. I didn't see whether anything appeared on the transcript [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, it wasn't recorded on the transcript, but should the Chamber decide that it needs to investigate, it will have to look at that tape. So I'm just marking the time to assist in that process.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We thank you for that assistance. We carry on with the testimony of the witness. Witness, this was an incident which was not foreseen. I hope it doesn't disturb you too much. If you are ready, Ms. Hasan would continue her examination.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I only would like to know who he addressed when he said, "Fuck your mothers." If that's possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that what he said as well, apart from saying that this were lies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. When he was going out. When he was leaving the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You mean when he was removed from the courtroom, yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I can imagine your question. Let's now try to focus again on the questions that are put to you by Ms. Hasan, and please answer them and try to focus. Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness, and thank you for your patience. Now we've been talking about this incident of a prisoner being shot at the Nova Kasaba football field. Can you tell us, in your words, what is -- as far as you remember it, what happened?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: Well, while Mladic was there, holding a speech, one of the youths stood up. I don't know why he stood up. At any rate, the Serbian soldiers removed him from the rows where we were seated. He was toward the end of the row. He started beating him with rifle-butts and kicking him, and then one of them shot him from a rifle. His body was thrown into a nearby ditch. Mladic was present but didn't react at all. We were told, they told us, that if anyone of us should behave this way, we would be killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. Now, after being held at the Nova Kasaba football field, where were you taken immediately after that?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: They put us on buses. The buses left for Konjevic Polje in the direction of Kravica. They brought us to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: After being taken in Bratunac and, as you've previously testified, you were held on a bus there near a school, you were subsequently taken to a school in Pilica; do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: How many nights were you held at the school in Pilica?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: Two nights.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And we have your evidence about your detention there as part of your Krstic testimony. I'd like to move to when you were then subsequently taken to the killing fields, as you describe them. And after the executions took place there, which you survived, you escaped to a bridge under which you hid for a day. And sometime after that, you encountered an older man who you continued your escape with. If we could just go into private session for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Apart from the time when your name was taken at Nova Kasaba, were you interviewed at any time during your capture?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: Can you repeat your question?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Apart -- apart from the time when you were at the Nova Kasaba football field, and you had testified that you had provided your name to the Serb soldiers there, were you at any other time during your captivity, since -- until the time you were released, interviewed?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: We were only registered in Kasaba. The -- we had to provide our dates of birth, and they were put on a list. This was at the place where Mladic held the speech.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: When you arrived at Batkovic camp, were you registered there?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Do you recall who registered you?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: The Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Had you been registered by the Red Cross before your arrival at Batkovic camp?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: If you recall, can you provide us the date that you arrived at the Batkovic camp?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: I think it was the 26th.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Of what month?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: July.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And do you know where the Batkovic camp was located?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is this in dispute, or would you think the witness to take a different view on the location of Batkovic camp?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I'm not sure if the Defence disputes this. If they don't, then there may be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Location of the Batkovic camp is not in dispute. You should have inquired. You have announced that would you need 30 minutes. So, therefore, use your time as efficient as possible. Because you're at 26.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: How many prisoners, Witness, were held at the Batkovic camp at the time you arrived, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: I'm not sure about the exact number.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness repeat the last thing he said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you repeat the last words you spoke. You said you were not sure about the exact number but ... Did you add anything?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The hangar there was full.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, Witness, do you remember taking an investigator of the Office of the Prosecutor of this Tribunal called Jean-Rene Ruez in 1999 to some of the locations you had been taken to during your captivity?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Can you tell us which places you remember going to?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: Yes. We went to the school where we were detained, to the place where I went to fetch water, and the place where we were shot.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have no more questions but I would like to move to offer in the associated exhibits with his Krstic and Karadzic testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Those being the photographs? No. Yes, associated exhibits. Photographs?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yes, there are a number of photographs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I have a list before me of eight photographs, or at least eight. First of all, Mr. Stojanovic, are there any objections against the eight photographs as listed?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections against admission. Then let's go through them rather quickly. Madam Registrar, 65 ter 04835, photograph, panoramic photo of Kravica warehouse.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Receives number P1120, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P1120 is admitted into evidence. Next one, 65 ter 05030, photograph, unannotated version of helicopter overview of the area, annotated to show execution site, water-pipe, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Receives number P1121, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence. 05049, photograph, helicopter view, Branjevo farm. And then the description continues with a few more details.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Receives number P1122, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P1122 is admitted. 65 ter 05248, photo exhibit book of Jean-Rene Ruez, page 213.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Receives number P1123, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. 28757, 65 ter, annotated photo of Kravica warehouse.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Receives number P1124, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. 65 ter 28758, annotated aerial photo of Pilica school marked by the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Receives number P1125, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted. 65 ter 28759, annotated photo of Pilica school.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Receives number P1126, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Yes, the description is identical to the previous one but apparently there are two aerial photos. Then the last one, 65 ter 28760, annotated aerial photo of Branjevo farm.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Receives number P1127, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Ms. Hasan, any further matter?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. In relation to P1123, which is 65 ter 5248, we will endeavour to just upload the single page. And there was a correction exhibit list sent out. The correct page is page 207. It can be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Page 207.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Correct. And that will be 65 ter 5248A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Because what I just read is also from the 10th of April, but apparently there is a more recent one then. It will be page 207 separately uploaded from the photo exhibit book. Any further matter?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: No. That's everything. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the 65 ter number is on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we start the cross-examination, Mr. Stojanovic, there are two matters the Chamber would like to briefly raise. First we'd like to ask one or two additional questions to you, Witness. You may have heard, you said, Mr. Mladic said aloud that you were telling lies. Now, Mr. Lukic said, told us that he heard Mr. Mladic say that it was just a - let me see - it was a learned story you told -- you had told us. Now, having heard that, is there any chance that you -- that did he not say that you were lying, or did you clearly hear use him the words "lie," or "liar," or "you are lying," or was it more the version as Mr. Lukic told us. I just want to check with you how accurate you heard, how certain you are about what you heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I make a suggestion. The witness speaks fluent English. And if it may assist the Chamber to avoid any kind of translation misinterpretation, perhaps the Chamber would be willing to hear him answer questions in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, of course, if you'd prefer to answer the question in English, but you're listening to the B/C/S channel, I take it, at this moment. Or are you listening to the English channel? I do not know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Bosnian. I'm sure what I heard, and I have no doubts about it. He said that that was made up, that those were lies. He used foul language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Foul language before he was removed from the courtroom, or you would say after we ordered him to be removed from the courtroom? I'm talking about the foul language.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. He swore while he was being taken out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] So even having heard what Mr. Lukic said, you have no doubt that he was talking about made-up stories. Did he use the word "lie," or "liar," or did he just limit himself to made-up stories?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He said that I made everything up and that I was lying. And I heard it with my own ears.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for those answers. Then for -- Mr. Lukic, as usual, Mr. Mladic is removed from the courtroom for the duration of the testimony of the witness, the testimony of the witness during whose testimony he misbehaved. So, therefore, it might be that we could conclude the testimony of this witness later this morning and start with the next witness. So, therefore, the removal of the courtroom, for the Court at least, doesn't mean that he necessarily should be transported back to the United Nations Detention Unit. I take it that Madam Registrar has overheard my conversation with you as well, Mr. Lukic. Mr. Lukic, if you're ready -- oh, Mr. Stojanovic, if you're ready to cross-examine the witness, you're invited to start. Witness, you'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Stojanovic. Mr. Stojanovic is counsel for Mr. Mladic. Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, are we going to take a break now? What is the procedure now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The procedure is that the short sessions are mainly to accommodate Mr. Mladic. Since Mr. Mladic is not in court, we have the usual sessions of one hour and a half. Please proceed. Which also would mean that if you are very efficient, that having 25 minutes left during this session, that perhaps in the next session, also in view of the assessment you gave on how much time you would need, that we would conclude in the next session, the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for these instructions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise sincerely for this incident and I regret your having been forced to experience it. I have a few questions for you. Up until the 11th of July, 1995, you were a member of the 28th Division of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina in the village where you resided; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what specific tasks you had as a member of the that unit, per establishment? Did you have any rank?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: No. I was just posted on the line. We were holding the line, and that was all.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What weapons did you have?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: Nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: At the time when you were discharging military duties, were you issued with automatic weapons?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So how were you discharging your military duties of securing the lines?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: While the area was not protected, there were a couple of rifles available, but after it became a safe haven, the rifles were seized. And after that, there were neither any lines, nor soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: After the zone was established, the protected zone, were you active as a member of the brigade?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In which activities were you involved after the protected area was established?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: I wasn't involved in anything. I was simply a refugee.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that from the area where you stayed, offensive activities were launched against the VRS territories in 1994 and 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We didn't hear the witness's answer because of the overlapping.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. The interpreters draw our attention to the fact that they did not hear the witness's answer and then you started already your next question. Is that the last portion of the answer which we see on the transcript? After where the witness said that he was simply a refugee, or is it already the answer to the next question?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The answer to the next question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please repeat your answer to the question, whether you know that from the area where you were staying, offensive activities were launched against the VRS territories in 1994 and 1995. Whether you are aware of that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic. And take a break after you've asked your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: On the 11th of July, an order arrived for the able-bodied men to proceed to the Jaglici village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Are you -- can you tell the Chamber, to the best of your knowledge, who issued the order to send the able-bodied men to Jaglici and women and children to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: I heard that from other people. But who originally issued this order, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In the village where you were staying, was there a military command that was capable of receiving and forwarding such an order?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: Zulfo was a former commander but I didn't hear anything personally from him. I heard it from other people. He was a commander there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "commander," are you talking about Zulfo Tursunovic? Am I right?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: Yes, you are.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please repeat your answer, because I don't think it's been recorded, and please wait a bit and after I have finished my question. Thank you. How long did it take you, and how many of you, left from the area where you had been to the village of Jaglici?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. I was in the group made up of some 10 or 15 people, and it took us about 45 minutes, up to an hour. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, could I invite you to look at your text screen, if it as -- and wait until it stops moving after a question has been put to you and only then answer it. Because there's an overlap in speakers, and our transcribers need time and our interpreters need time to give us the right information. Mr. Stojanovic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Upon arrival in Jaglici, did you see armed military formations and soldiers of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: When I arrived in Jaglici, there were between 10.000 and 15.000 people. I'm not sure whether some of them were armed or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you be more specific when you say you're not sure? You saw them or you didn't see them?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection, while passing in -- in the column, which task you were given? What were you told about your destination?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: We were told that we were going to Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know that that was the VRS-controlled territory?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: Which territory are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The territory through which the column was passing towards Tuzla, did that involve the passage beyond the Srebrenica enclave and the passage through the territory controlled by the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you aware that this area was mined?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: No. But I was able to notice that there were mines planted there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Who personally directed these activities? And who led you towards Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: Nobody led me. I headed on my way along with all the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection, on the route before you were captured, how many people from the column perished?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: At one location, I saw four or five dead bodies, people who were killed. Then the next location, near Kamenica, there was an ambush there. There was a tree that had been felled and there were about 300 dead there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you, at any point, exposed to shooting?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: Yes. The whole time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did somebody get killed while passing through the minefields?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see if anyone committed suicide?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: I'm not sure. It is possible, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection, please tell the Chamber more specifically where the Kamenica location is, where you saw about 300 dead bodies.

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: I am not quite sure if you walk through the forest from Jaglici towards Kamenica, I don't know the exact location because I had never been there before.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. To the best of your recollection, on the 13th of July, you said that you were captured on the morning of that day. Can you tell the Court an approximate time when you were taken prisoner?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: It may have been at around 7.00. I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You don't know if you were captured by the military or the police.

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: No, I'm not sure. I think it was the military.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So, from 7.00, according to your estimate, until 1400 hours, that's the time you spent in the school; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court how many of you were in this school in total and how many of you walked or were taken on foot to the football pitch in Kasaba?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: I think that there were ten people. And then they captured another man in the vicinity of the school. That makes a total of 11, but I'm not quite sure. And then all of us were then returned to the football pitch.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let us now deal with an issue that we deem to be significant. According to your estimate, when you were brought to the football pitch - and that was between 1400 hours, or, let's say, at around 1400 hours, if I'm not mistaken - how many people were there?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: Between 1500 and 2.000.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with your leave, I would kindly that the document that I'm going to use be under seal. So can we please have document 1D870 in e-court. That's the witness's statement given on the 20th of July, 1996, to the State Commission for the Collection of Facts Relating to War Crimes. And I would draw your attention to page number 2 in the B/C/S and in English as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The last paragraph, where you say: "At the stadium, there was a large number of prisoners, both civilians and soldiers. I think that we numbered several hundred people and the number kept growing as they were bringing people from all directions whom they had captured in the surrounding area." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: This is my question for you. When, a moment ago, you said that, in your estimate, at the time of your arrival, there were between 1.500 and 2.000 people, was that a number that -- of people that you saw there when you got there, or was it the number of people at the time when you were being transported?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: I think that referred to the time when we were still there. There were other people still arriving.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: From the point when you got there and until the point when General Mladic appeared there, were there other prisoners brought over?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let's have a look at a portion of the transcript of your evidence in the Karadzic case.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we call up in e-court page 35 of the transcript from the Karadzic case, which I believe was today assigned the number P --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P1119, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 35, line 5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we -- could you assist us in giving the page number in the previous case, the Karadzic case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And for the transcript, it's P1119.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's page 35 in e-court, line 5. And page 24146. That's the transcript page from the Karadzic case. 24146.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, there are only five pages in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: If I can just assist, it's because, I believe, that's only what we uploaded, the excerpts we proffered into evidence. So this portion of the Karadzic transcripts would not be included but perhaps it can be read out.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Your Honours, then, with your leave, we have uploaded it. It's 1D867. 1D867. Can we have page 35 in e-court, then. It corresponds to page 24146.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can I direct your attention to line 5. Sir, in the Karadzic case, you also spoke about this issue, and you said that, at the time, that the number of people who were present at the football field grew to about 2- or 3.000 people. You see that?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Today you told us that, to the best of your knowledge, there were between 1.500 and 2.000 people. So in your view what would be the most accurate figure?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: Well, I don't know exactly. I did say when I was testifying in the Karadzic case that it was between 2- or 3.000. There may have been even been 4.000 people. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'll ask to you look at a document, which is 65 ter 28756. It's a collection of photographs which we plan to use with the next witness. And I'd like us to look at page 43 of the document. That's to say, the photograph on that page. Sir --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, for the transcript, let me say that this is one of the photographs from the collection we received from the Prosecution. It's dated the 13th of July, 1995, 1400 hours, precisely at the time that the witness referred to as having been brought over to the football pitch and that would be the time when the number of people that he mentioned were there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, it's not very common that someone who is not examining the witness intervenes, but if there's any special reason, please tell us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, and I do it reluctantly, Your Honour, and -- but because we are out of sequence, I wanted to point out this is an aerial image provided pursuant to Rule 70 by the United States. It is open and been used many times, as we know. But I just wanted to clarify that this squiggly mark next to 1400 hours is told to us by the United States to mean about 1400 hours. We were going to be getting into that with Mr. Ruez a bit, but I just wanted to clear that up for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, the 1400 hours is preceded by a small sign, which, as I understand, is often used to indicate that it is an approximate indication and not a precise one. I take it that the clarification is helpful. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I do accept that that is the case. And I did say that it corresponded to what the witness had said. He did say that he was brought over to this place at about 1400 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise this area?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Will you agree with me that this is an aerial image of the football pitch at Nova Kasaba?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Are you able to see the disposition of people who were either seated or standing in the field in these two groups?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: Well, I think that this group over here was seated; whereas this other was standing. I'm not sure. It is an aerial image, after all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, it would be not be on the record what this group over here or the other group would be. We have a group which seems to be a rather thin line going from down -- from -- from bottom to the top in more vertical direction, and we have a bigger more rectangular, almost a square, group of prisoners. Which one you remember to have been seated, and which one was standing, in your view? If -- if you remember. If not, please tell us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know that I was seated, and I think that I was in this larger group. I'm not sure about the other group.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The larger group meaning the one more in the middle of the football field.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stojanovic, I'm looking at the clock. We -- if this would be a suitable moment for a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We take a break, and we'll resume at 11.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For the witness to re-enter the courtroom, we have to move into closed session for a second.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Stojanovic, once the curtains are up again, you may resume your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, if you recall, we stopped when we were discussing the photograph that you have now in front of you. Can I ask you again so that we can confirm, to the best of your recollection, roughly an hour after your arrival at the football pitch in Kasaba, Ratko Mladic arrived. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: At the point when General Mladic arrived, were you seated or were you standing?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: We were seated.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'd like to us look at the next paragraph now. It's 65 ter 28756, the same document, the same collection but a different photograph, at page 44. It is a magnified image.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you a couple of things. Can you help us with this: You were seated in such a way that you were facing the lower or the bottom part of the photograph, or, rather, the direction facing the road leading to Konjevic Polje; right?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: Yes. I was facing this group, the other group that was there.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Can we have the usher's assistance now to hand the pen to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And, Witness, to the best of your recollection, can you draw a circle indicating the area where you were seated, approximately, at the point of General Mladic's arrival.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, before we do so, let me try to clarify one thing. You said, asking about which direction the witness was facing, whether he was facing in the direction of the road. That means more to the bottom of the photograph. The witness said: "I was facing the other group." Which is -- may -- it at least creates some ambiguity. Because the other group is, from this larger group, not in the direction of the road, but, rather, in a different direction. So before you ask the witness to mark where he was, or after that, could you ask him to mark with an arrow which direction he was facing when being seated so that we know, for sure, in which direction it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for your assistance. I think that it is only proper to do it this way. I was wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please, Witness, when marking the area where you were, draw an arrow that will indicate the way you were facing.

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you now draw a circle to indicate the spot where you were when General Mladic arrived, to the best of your recollection. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the sake of the transcript, let me say that the witness drew an irregular circle in the central part of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you place number 1 next to it.

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: That would indicate the spot where you were. Now I'd like to ask you to draw a circle to indicate the spot where General Mladic was when he addressed you.

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please write "RM" next to that circle.

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At the time when General Ratko Mladic arrived, do you remember there being some UNPROFOR or UN vehicles there?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell Their Honours how many such vehicles there were, that you recall?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: There was one UN vehicle. I think it was an APC, I'm not sure. There were Serbian APCs. I do want to say that this is where, roughly, the military APC was, this is where the army was, but this image doesn't reflect that at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I will ask you, however, to place "OT" next to that circle, which would stand for "armoured carrier." And next to the line that you drew, can you just write the army, "V"?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And then, if you can recall, can you mark the spot on this image where the UN armoured carrier was?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: It was roughly in this area.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you place "UN" next to it.

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: On his arrival, General Ratko Mladic addressed you from the spot that you've just marked.

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And he told you that you would all be exchanged; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: He also told you that it wasn't possible at all for you to break your way through to Tuzla because there were quite a few ambushes and obstacles in the way; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: He said that nobody would be able to pass, not even a bird, that nobody would be able to advance not even for 100 metres [as interpreted]. And as far as I know, there was no attempt at breaking through that area anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm being told that in line 14 of the transcript what the witness said was misconstrued. It was said here that it was 100 metres, whereas the witness said -- or perhaps I could resolve this through a question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you just tell Their Honours, to the best of your recollection, what did exactly General Mladic say to you apart from the fact that you would be exchanged?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: Okay. When General Mladic came, he addressed us. He said that we would all be exchanged, that we would be having lunch in Bratunac, that he would organise groups that would go out into the hills and woods to collect the wounded. All those who were killed would be buried. He ordered that a list of all of us who were there be drawn. He designated a group of some four to five soldiers to register everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And when he said that he would send you all off to Bratunac for lunch, were there any comments made?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember if, at the time, there were wounded individuals among you at the football pitch in Kasaba?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: Yes, there were wounded people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, before you put the last question, you apparently had some concerns about the transcript and about the 100 metres. Now if that concern exists, it has been -- not been resolved. Perhaps I ask the following question. Witness, you said something about that Mr. Mladic told you that you wouldn't make it very far, and, in that context, the transcript tells us that you mentioned 100 metres. Could you tell us what that -- whether that accurately reflects what you said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. He said that there were 100 lines between that place and Tuzla and that not even a bird can fly over.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is now clear. Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, do you remember if the Serbian soldiers provided first aid to the wounded people?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please explain to the Court what you saw and how they provided this assistance.

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: I saw them bandaging people who were wounded. They were putting bandages on them. That's what I recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: That was the time while General Mladic was still there.

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: I think so. I'm not sure, but I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You were also offered a possibility to use some water. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You're also not sure whether the list drawn up on that occasion containing the number of people on the pitch was finalised before the departure of General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: How long did those five people take to make up the list of the people in -- on the pitch in Kasaba?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: I don't know, but I remember that as people were leaving the column their names were taken down. If I remember correctly, there was a table. Everyone had to pass by that table, give their name and date of birth, and then board the bus.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the last sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So this registering --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. The witness is invited to repeat the last part of his previous answer. "Everyone had to pass by that table," you said, "give their name and date of birth, and then board the bus." And what did you say after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After that, when the buses were full, some people were left behind on the pitch, after me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So this list was made while people were boarding the buses. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: Yes, I think you are.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: At that location, General Mladic was no longer there. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: No, I'm not sure. I think he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection, how long did he stay there?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: I am not sure. Perhaps an hour. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: But please, can you be of assistance. You said that you arrived at around 1400 hours. One hour later, according to your estimate, which is to say at around 1500 hours, General Mladic arrived.

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So he stayed for an hour, that is to say, up until 1600 hours. I put to you that in all the cases where you testified, you said that you headed for Bratunac by buses in the evening hours. Where have these minimum four hours -- have gone?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: Four hours? Well, I don't know when we set off exactly. I just said approximately that it was dark when we reached Bratunac. Now what time exactly it was, I don't know. I didn't have a watch with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I understand that. But, please, surely you set off towards Bratunac at dusk or in the early evening hours, as was stated in one of your testimonies. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: Yes. We set off before it got dark. Maybe an hour before. I don't know exactly. Because once we arrived in Bratunac, it was already in dark.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: All right. I'm asking you this because I would like to remind you and ask you if you still stand by your statement that, to the best of your estimate -- remained there for about an hour [as interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. Not one hour. He wasn't there when I arrived. Maybe it was an hour later that he came.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: But you stand by your statement that he stayed there about 60 minutes or one hour.

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, just to be clear on the record, the witness previously said to your question how long did he stay there, his answer was: "I'm not sure. Perhaps an hour. I don't know exactly." So the witness indicated that he was not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. That is why I repeated the question because I realised that when I said one hour, the witness understood this to be 1300 hours in the afternoon and that he arrived at around 1400 hours, and I think that that is the reason for this slight confusion in the transcript, but I hope that we have clarified this. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, in the photograph that is in front of you, can you please put an arrow indicating the place where the soldier - and I would kindly ask the usher to assist the witness - the location where the soldier -- or the prisoner was taken from the group that you mentioned. Can you put an arrow of the direction.

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: It's here, in this part. This is where he was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how far that was from the place where you were?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but not too far, because I was able to see everything that was going on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, first of all, often, if you want a marking of a spot or a place rather than a direction, you better not use an arrow, which the witness wisely then did not do. The place approximately where the soldier was -- was, was taken out, is marked by the witness with a small circle, just right and up from where he marked the presence of a UN vehicle. And perhaps he could add something like, soldier, or P, for prisoner. That -- if you could mark the place with a P for prisoner.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, there it is. Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us, in your memory, can you tell us what kind of weapon did the soldier use to shoot this prisoner?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: I am not sure. I think it was a pistol. I know that he was beaten with a rifle-butt. And then one of the soldiers put -- took out a handgun and shot him dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me if you had an impression that this prisoner exhibited some uncontrolled behaviour?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did he leave an impression of being psychologically distressed?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: I don't know. All I know is that he stood up, said something, and then he was singled out and beaten up.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with your leave, can we please enter the photograph with the markings into evidence because I'm going to move onto other exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But before we do so, I'd like to add one question. Witness, looking at the arrow you marked on this photograph, and looking at the place where you said Ratko Mladic was, do I understand you well that you were not directly facing him but that you had to look to your left to see him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Registrar, the number to be assigned to the photograph marked by the witness would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Would be D269, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D269 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we remove it from the screen, Judge Fluegge has a follow-up question as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Witness, during the examination-in-chief you were asked about the behaviour of General Mladic when this prisoner was killed. And you said: "Mladic was present but didn't react at all. We were told, they told us, that if any one of us should behave this way, we would be killed." You said, "We were told, they told us," who are "they"? Who told you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Serb soldiers. In fact, the same soldiers that killed that man.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with your leave, can we look again at document 1D870. That's the witness's statement given on the 20th of July, 1996.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not to be shown to the public.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I please have -- yes, it's under the seal because we already used it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stojanovic, it is -- the statement is not in evidence at this moment, is it? So, therefore, if you once said it is not to be shown to the public, that does not make it an exhibit under seal. So, therefore, you should repeat it whenever you use it. And even if it were an exhibit under seal, then it's always good to remind us that it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we please look at page 2, last paragraph in the B/C/S; and I think it's page 3, first paragraph, in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can we please look at it together. A while ago, you said that you were not under the impression that this man had some mental problems, the prisoner. In your statement given on the 20th of July, 1996, you said something different, and you said on that occasion, which is a year after the event: "I personally saw one of the captured civilians, probably psychologically distressed, stood up, straightened up, because we all had to sit down in the stadium, and then four Chetniks approached him, forced him to sit down by kicking him and hitting them with their fists, and then one of them shot him dead with a pistol."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I'm just looking at page 2 of the English which I think is probably where the reference is. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it is --

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: In the English version it says nothing about any psychological disturbance of any sort. It just simply --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it says "probably due to shattered nerves."

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yeah. "The civilian stood up, probably due to shattered nerves ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: That says nothing about his state of mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me -- if you give me one second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please, Mr. Stojanovic. Well, Mr. Stojanovic, could you please be very clear. Make a clear distinction between having a mental problem, which I understand, but perhaps you'd verify with the witness how he understood that, whether it was someone with some -- with some psychological disorder of any kind and, on the other hand, shattered nerves due to a situation, which might shatter perhaps everyone's nerves. Could you make a clear distinction between the two, rather than to ask for an explanation of what you present, more or less, as a contradiction, which might not be fully fair to the witness. So would you please keep this in mind when further exploring this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, since you speak the language of the statement put to you, it says here that you said and signed the following: "One of the prisoners, probably due to psychologically being distraught ..." Now I'm asking you do you stand by this; and, if you do, how do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure what actually occurred. He got up, but why he got up, I really don't know. And why they beat him UP and then eventually killed him, I don't know. It's irrelevant. I don't know why they killed him. It's totally unclear to me. I don't know what else to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: On the basis of what did you make a conclusion that he was probably mentally distraught?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: Well, my conclusion was based on the fact that we all were forced to sit down, whereas he got up. And that indicated to me that something was wrong with him because everybody else had to remain sitting and didn't dare get up.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did he shout?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: I don't remember. He was talking. I don't know what about.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Was he threatening?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did he try to hit anyone of these people?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You're not sure if General Mladic was able to see it all?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: Well, he was there. He should have been able to see what was happening. I think you'd best ask him. He was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you this because --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your leave, Your Honours, I'd like to suggest that we look at document 1D868 in e-court. Let me note that it's under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: It's the statement that you gave, Witness, on the 11th of March, 1996, to AID, the Agency for Investigation and Documentation, the Tuzla office. I'd like us to look at the first paragraph, where you talk about this event and say that you arrived at the field or the pitch at around 1400 hours. At the field in Djugum, the Chetniks first kicked and punched and rifle-butted a youth whom they killed. "I did not know the young man, but he was dark, tall, and about 30 years old". You then say that you were addressed by Ratko Mladic, and then you mention the words that you've already told us here. Does this refresh your recollection that in fact this incident happened before Mladic's arrival at Kasaba?

utterances.speaker: RM346
utterances.text: No. It didn't happen before. Mladic was already there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, where do you get it from, from this statement, that Mr. Mladic had not arrived yet?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. On the basis of the documents that I intend to adduce through the witnesses that we will call, but that's why I wanted to clear up the statement, first of all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But you're referring to this statement to make that assertion, and that -- this statement doesn't make that assertion. Then you can make that assertion without referring to this statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I thought that I would clear up this issue with the witness through this document. I thought this would jog his memory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
